_comment: What each hull is good and bad against, in the world's own voice. Sean, 19 September: "Delete the description text that repeats the stats... Replace it with 1-2 sentences of in-world flavor text per ship that tells the player what the ship is good and bad against, naturally." The roster's own Design Notes column said 'Heavy Armor 22; 400 Hull; 7 Long and 8 Heavy Guns' - which is the stat grid again, in a sentence. Kept in its own file rather than added to combat-ships.json, because that file carries a standing instruction to be changed by re-reading the sheet and never by hand: a line written in there would be gone the next time the roster is imported. Keyed by Ship ID, and a test fails if a hull ever has no line or a line has no hull.

flavour.CFS-BLA-R6-01: Twelve light guns is a hail of shot, and against bare timber it is murder. Put her in front of anything properly plated and every one of them rings off the iron.
flavour.CFS-BRI-S02: A merchantman with two guns bolted on and two troops below: she is for getting them there, not for what happens when she arrives. Anything built to fight will take her.
flavour.CWN-BUL-R3-01: Armor twenty-five and seven hundred of hull — light guns break on her all day and she does not much notice. She cannot catch anything, and a fast ship that keeps its distance will find the seams eventually.
flavour.CFS-CHI-S03: Well plated for her size and cheap to keep, which makes her a nuisance to shift off a harbor mouth. She has almost nothing to shoot with, so she wins by lasting rather than by hitting.
flavour.CFS-COR-R8-01: Armor twenty-nine, guns of all three kinds, and she grows back between actions what you take off her. Only a Majestic out-shoots her, and even that is a long afternoon's work.
flavour.CFS-CUT-R2-01: Two heavy guns on a small hull is more than anything her size has a right to carry, and plated sloops have learned to fear her. Her own plating is thin, and she is not quick enough to leave when it goes badly.
flavour.CWN-INT-S02: Ninety of hull and no armor at all: she is built to be hard to hit rather than hard to sink, and a heavy gun misses her nine times in ten. The tenth ends her.
flavour.CWN-INT-R5-02: Fifteen guns on something that cannot be hit, five of them reaching before anybody else fires. Everything she has is in that first exchange; a hull that survives it will go straight through her.
flavour.CFS-IRB-R5-01: Eight long guns and a wall-breaking eight of bombardment: she opens the action a mile out and opens harbors from the same distance. Let anything close and she has one heavy gun to answer with.
flavour.CWN-JUS-R6-01: Twenty-four guns across all three kinds, so nothing she meets is the wrong sort of target. Four hundred of hull is modest for a large ship and she carries nobody, so she can beat an island and never take one.
flavour.CWN-MAJ-R8-01: The only armor thirty afloat and the heaviest battery in either navy; one to one there is nothing she cannot out-shoot. She is slow enough that two ships will always choose the fight, and two is what it takes.
flavour.CFS-MAR-R1-01: Fast, cheap, and carrying two troops: she is for undefended harbors and lone merchantmen. A warship of any size will finish her in one exchange.
flavour.CWN-MOR-S03: Eight heavy guns go through anything the early war puts in front of her, and twenty-four armor means little comes back. She costs more to keep than she is worth by the time the better hulls open.
flavour.CFS-REE-R4-01: Seven heavy guns is a capital-killer's battery on a hull costing a fraction of one. Three hundred and fifty of hull is the price: she wins quickly or she does not win.
flavour.CWN-RES-R2-01: Quick, cheap to lay down, and useful at everything without being the answer to anything. Against a real warship her best work is being somewhere else.
flavour.CWN-SOV-S04: Nine hundred of hull and six troops in her belly: this is how the Crown takes an island on the first morning. Slow, with no long guns at all, so she arrives having already been shot at.
flavour.CWN-SOV-R7-02: The same idea with the faults taken out — fourteen heavy guns, six long, and quick enough to choose her fight. Short of a Majestic there is nothing she ought to lose to.
flavour.CFS-SWI-S01: No guns, no armor and seventy of hull: she is a pair of eyes and nothing else. Anything at all will sink her, so the whole trick is never being where it is.
flavour.CFS-TEM-R3-01: Four long guns and eighteen of armor on a fast medium hull — she hits first, hard, and shrugs off the answer. A hundred and seventy-five of hull means the second exchange is not hers.
flavour.CFS-TID-S04: She mends herself between actions, which makes her very hard to grind down over a campaign. Six armor means one heavy broadside undoes a fortnight of it.
flavour.CFS-URG-R7-01: Eighteen hundred of hull, more than anything else afloat, and nine troops to put on a beach. One loses to a Majestic; two do not, and the Confederacy can build two.
flavour.CWN-VAN-R1-01: Five hundred of hull and eleven guns for the price of a medium: the hull the Crown lays down when it wants ships rather than a ship. Nothing about her frightens a capital.
flavour.CWN-VAN-R4-02: The same bargain, better in every column — seven hundred of hull, twenty-four armor, sixteen guns. She still carries no long guns, so somebody who does will always get the first word.
flavour.CWN-WAY-S01: Four troops and a chart table, with two guns for politeness. She is how the Crown finds an island and how it settles one; she is not how it keeps one.
